chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding an aunt who came to dispute the mawla (client) of a man who had died.
And those of kinship among each other have nearer proximity in the prescription of Allah.
So he gave the inheritance to the aunt and did not give it to the mawla.

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ: More entitled to each other / have closer claim

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali rule on inheritance between an aunt and a mawla based on Quranic kinship?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) application of the principle of *al-rahim* (kinship) in inheritance jurisprudence, prioritizing the maternal aunt over the *mawla* (client) based on Quran 8:75. This ruling is significant in Shia scholarship as it highlights the precedence of blood ties (*dhawu al-arham*) over the socio-legal bond of clientage (*mawali*) when determining inheritance shares. It underscores the flexibility of the Imam’s legal reasoning in integrating Quranic verses with pre-Islamic and early Islamic customs to establish equitable distribution.
